summary: Set 108 Session 1 of 4 settled everything Sessions 2-4 depend on, and its distinguishing choice was to establish facts by RUNNING things rather than by reading source. Both service contracts (`POST /convert`, `POST /batches`) were captured as literal wire bodies from real services started on this machine - status codes, envelopes, error bodies and the `Location` header are transcriptions, not descriptions. All four rows of watcher's decision table were forced live, including a deferred file retried and stored on a later tick. Part D was proven twice: once with a falsifier (the original converter killed while the watcher kept working), and once with BOTH dependencies moved to the 52xx band and 5101/5102 confirmed unreachable, the batch read back through the alternate persistence. The nine-module Work Explorer POC was re-confirmed against the running product at two levels: an on-disk suite driving the product's own manifest parser, session-set discovery and grouping (5 passing), and a rendered-DOM suite that loads the shipping client.js into headless Chromium and asserts on actual treeitem rows, aria-levels and document order (4 passing). Deliverables: `s1-service-contracts.md` and `s1-walk-outline.md` (rulings R1-R9, four parts with behavioural finish lines, the ownership table, and the handover). Three rulings deliberately depart from the spec's prose and are flagged for Step 9: R1 revises the POC's `converter-v1` naming (version-in-slug needs central version allocation, contradicting 'nobody waits on anybody'; settled by a two-engine consult that converged); R8b corrects the success criterion's 'nothing but the .NET 10 SDK' - the happy path needs Windows plus LocalDB, both verified on this machine; and the spec's Parts table states test counts as finish lines, which is unusable for readers whose AI generates a different test decomposition. VERIFICATION: six rounds, closing VERIFIED with 0 findings (discovery fan-out 2/2, supplementary, remediation-review x4; rounds 5 and 6 operator-authorised past the 2-cycle bound, which the loop respected by suspending rather than re-opening on its own authority). Eleven distinct Major findings, all accepted, none disputed - eight from the original draft and THREE introduced by the remediation itself and caught by the fix-delta review. An operator-authorised third-provider opinion (gemini-2.5-pro, with both anthropic and openai excluded) adjudicated round 5 'both partly right', judged the loop converging rather than salience-churning, and found a Major that six rounds had missed: two members' persistence services would share one hardcoded LocalDB database and collide on EF migrations mid-Part-D. R5 now allocates a database name per member alongside the port bands. The most instructive failure was a disclosure aimed at the wrong audience - the shared database WAS disclosed, but only as a limit on this session's proof, and the note then told Session 2 that nothing in the tutorial sets one up; it read like care and functioned as shipping a defect.

reason.specifics: Session 2 writes the tutorial against R1-R9 plus two contracts' worth of literal captured strings, and must hold every one of them across a long document without paraphrasing. Literal fidelity under length is exactly what this session's routed drafts were weakest at, and it is the failure Session 4's human walk cannot recover from - a reader who types a command that does not exist stops. The routed analyst recommended the same engine; its stated reason (justifying an exception to the budget constraint) was backwards, since anthropic is the operator-invoked engine here and a provider switch is the cost, not the default. The fresh-eyes reading a switch would buy is supplied instead by the mandatory cross-provider verification with anthropic excluded, and by routing S2's duplicate-procedure grep off-provider. Second choice if the operator prefers provider diversity: openai / gpt-5-6, effort high.
